label.independent: Measured by an organization that does not sell the model or product (Epoch AI, Artificial Analysis, Arena, ARC Prize, METR, UK AISI, PJM's market monitor, Ramp's transaction data, an affected party's own incident record).
label.lab-reported: A company's own figure about its own model or its own work (labs, and companies speaking about themselves on stage or in a schedule abstract).
label.secondary: No primary page confirmed it; known only from aggregators or press.
label.official: A primary official record: a government text, a company's own launch page or filing, an official schedule, a platform's own counter.
label.estimate: A modelled estimate, or our own reading or arithmetic over the evidence.

verified.live: Re-read on the public page on 18 Nov 2026 (checkedAt gives the time).

compute-72-us.claim: Epoch AI's customs-based estimate puts 72% of the AI computing power delivered since 2022 in the US and about 10% in China (counting China's own chips).

compute-72-us.label: independent

source.title: Introducing the AI chip imports explorer

compute-72-us.caveat: An estimate built from customs data, through June 2026 (27.4M H100-equivalents).

runrate-105.claim: The State of AI Report puts OpenAI's and Anthropic's combined revenue run rate at $105B by late summer 2026, up from about $30B early in the year.

runrate-105.caveat: Lab-reported run rates relayed by the report, not audited revenue.

anthropic-s1.caveat: Share count and price range not set on the page.

capex-720.label: secondary

source.title: Big Tech AI capex: Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon and the spending race

capex-720.caveat: Secondary aggregator; not checked against company filings.

ramp-568.claim: 56.8% of US businesses in Ramp's sample paid for AI in October 2026, up 13.3 points in a year.
ramp-568.label: independent

source.title: Ramp AI Index

ramp-568.caveat: Sample of 85,000+ US businesses on Ramp; only paid tools are visible; not representative of all US firms (Census survey readings are far lower, ~a quarter of firms using AI).

ramp-volume-29.claim: In Ramp's data, token volume rose 29.0% and token spend 10.5% in the four weeks to 1 Nov 2026, while blended prices fell 14.8%.
ramp-volume-29.label: independent

source.title: Ramp AI Index

ramp-volume-29.caveat: Token data only from Ramp's AI spend-management users.

tokenmaxxing.claim: A backlash against “tokenmaxxing” (chasing AI usage metrics) emerged: Amazon's 27 Oct engineering guidance reportedly calls usage metrics “deeply flawed” when cut off from results. Spending did not fall: Ramp shows token spend still rising.
tokenmaxxing.label: press

source.title: Amazon tokenmaxxing AI engineering guidance

tokenmaxxing.caveat: Amazon's own document was not found; known from press. The backlash is a change in how firms judge usage, not a fall in spending.

eu-ai-act-aug.claim: EU AI Act enforcement began on 2 Aug 2026, with new duties to tell users they are dealing with a chatbot and to label deepfakes.
eu-ai-act-aug.label: official

source.title: Commission starts enforcing AI Act rules and new transparency requirements on 2 August

eu-ai-act-aug.caveat: AI-generated content must also carry machine-readable marks.

china-companion.claim: China's interim measures on anthropomorphic (companion-style) AI took effect on 15 Jul 2026 and forbid excessively catering to users or inducing emotional dependence or addiction.
china-companion.label: official

source.title: Interim Measures on Anthropomorphic AI Interactive Services (Xinhua)

china-companion.caveat: State media report of the rule; wording translated from Chinese.

eo-14434.claim: US Executive Order 14434 (29 Sep 2026) has federal agencies say “Super Intelligence” in place of “Artificial Intelligence”; it binds no private developer.
eo-14434.label: official

source.title: Executive Order 14434, Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence (91 FR 63129)

eo-14434.caveat: Terminology order for agencies; the binding US step on compute is the BIS export rule.
